**Binary SQLite backup as a second defense layer** (`scripts/backup-binary.mjs`). Full DB snapshot via `better-sqlite3`'s online backup API (`db.backup(destPath)`). Captures everything: user data, schema, WAL state, and `__drizzle_migrations` (so the backup survives schema changes — the JSON export drops anything not in its hardcoded table list, which is the bug below). Verifies via `PRAGMA integrity_check` on the copy; asserts the expected 5 user-facing tables are present. Module exports `runBackup()` for testability.

**Daily binary backup on the Pi** (`systemd/budget-tracker-binary-backup.{service,timer}`). Runs at 03:00 daily, 1 hour after the JSON export at 02:00, as the `budget` user (`Type=oneshot`). Picked up by the existing `deploy.sh` systemd rsync step (the deploy script already globs `systemd/`).

**Backup test suite** (`tests/server/backup.test.ts`, 8 integration tests): backup file has all 5 user-facing tables; backup is a valid SQLite file with the same data; binary captures `__drizzle_migrations`; `runBackup` throws if source DB missing; export produces a v1.1 snapshot with all 5 tables; export handles empty DBs; export + backup both pass `integrity_check`; failure path (corrupt backup) is detected.

**Production security headers on every response** (`server/middleware/99.security-headers.ts` + `server/utils/csp.ts`). Runs last, so the headers also land on 401 / 403 / 500 responses. Sets: `Content-Security-Policy` (or `-Report-Only` — see below), `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` (Funnel already does this; belt-and-suspenders), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()`. The policy is built in `server/utils/csp.ts:buildCsp({isDev, enforce})` and emitted by the middleware.

**CSP ships as `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` by default**, with `NUXT_CSP_ENFORCE=true` flipping it to enforcing. Reason: ECharts uses `new Function()` internally for some formatter features, so the prod policy may need `'unsafe-eval'`. The first deploy after this PR runs as Report-Only — open every dashboard chart (donut, cash-flow, daily-spends), watch the browser console for violations, then flip to enforcing once clean. Vite HMR in dev needs `'unsafe-eval'`, so dev always gets it; prod gets the stricter policy.

**CSRF middleware on state-changing `/api/*` requests** (`server/middleware/00.csrf.ts` + `server/utils/csrf.ts`). Runs first (before auth), so cross-origin state-changing requests are rejected with 403 before any DB lookup. Strategy: check the `Origin` header against a server-side allowlist (`NUXT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, comma-separated). Browsers always set `Origin` on `POST`/`PATCH`/`PUT`/`DELETE` and a cross-site attacker cannot spoof it (same-origin policy + CORS preflight), so this requires **zero client changes** — Nuxt's `$fetch` (ofetch) doesn't need a custom header. Exemptions: `GET`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS` (safe methods), `/api/auth/*` (login + setup-pin + future recover so they still work cross-origin during bootstrapping), non-`/api/*` paths. The dev default allowlist is `http://localhost:3000`; **production MUST set `NUXT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` explicitly** — the middleware rejects every state-changing request when the allowlist is empty in production.

**Security middleware test suites** (`tests/server/csrf.test.ts` — 17 tests, `tests/server/csp.test.ts` — 11 tests). CSRF: `parseAllowedOrigins` edge cases (empty, whitespace, duplicates) + `isOriginAllowed` (exact match, case sensitivity, missing origin, partial-match defense). CSP: `buildCsp` shape (dev vs prod, enforce vs report-only, the `unsafe-eval` decision, `frame-ancestors`, `object-src 'none'`).

**Silent data loss in JSON backup (`scripts/export.mjs` / `scripts/import.ts`).** The export shipped in v1.0.0 hardcoded a 4-table list (`users`, `accounts`, `categories`, `transactions`) and silently dropped `user_settings` — added in v1.1.0 (migration `0001`). Any `budget.db` restored from a pre-v1.6.0 JSON snapshot lost the primary account, the monthly budget, and per-user preferences, with no warning. `scripts/export.mjs` now exports the 5th table (snapshot version bumped 1.0 → 1.1); `scripts/import.ts` accepts the new `userSettings` field, defaults to `[]` for v1.0 snapshots (backward compat), and the wipe + insert order is updated to respect the `user_settings → accounts` FK (`users` → `accounts` → `categories` → `user_settings` → `transactions`).

**No `PRAGMA integrity_check` on the export path.** The export now opens the source DB with a separate `Database` instance, runs `integrity_check` before writing the JSON, and exits non-zero on `not ok`. A corrupt source DB no longer silently ships to Drive.
**`composables/useAccountBalances.ts`** — hoisted a `Map<id, account>` for O(1) type lookups (was O(n) per transaction). Refactor motivated by the `accountBalances.test.ts` golden-sums suite.
**`utils/dates.ts`** — new file. `localISODate` + `localMonthKey` moved out of `server/api/dashboard.get.ts` (shared across server + client).

**`server/utils/dashboardPeriods.ts`** — new module, extracted from `server/api/dashboard.get.ts`. The `since_last_salary` resolver now takes a `FindSalaryDate` callback so the chain is pure (no DB dependency in the unit test).

**CI actions bumped to `@v5`.** `actions/checkout`, `pnpm/action-setup`, `actions/cache` all pin `using: node24` (the v4 versions were being force-upgraded to Node 24 by the runner and emitting "Node 20 is being deprecated" warnings). `pnpm/action-setup@v5` keeps the same `package_json_file` input we rely on.

**`pnpm/action-setup` no longer takes an explicit `version`.** `package.json` pins `pnpm@9.12.0` via `packageManager`; passing both produces `ERR_PNPM_BAD_PM_VERSION`. Let the action read `packageManager` and stay single-source-of-truth.
**CI triggers widened from just `main` to `main` + `phase1/**`.** Direct pushes to phase1 branches also run CI without needing a PR first.

**Nitro middleware order pinned by filename prefix** (`server/middleware/00.csrf.ts`, `server/middleware/01.auth.ts`, `server/middleware/99.security-headers.ts`). The previous `server/middleware/auth.ts` is renamed to `01.auth.ts` so the three middlewares have a deterministic order: CSRF first (rejects cross-origin state changes before any DB lookup), auth second (still the global gate), security headers last (so they apply to error responses too, not just 2xx). If you add a new middleware, name it with a number prefix to keep the order explicit.

**Action required post-deploy**: any pre-v1.6.0 JSON snapshot in the local exports directory or in Google Drive is now considered stale (missing `user_settings`). Re-export once after the v1.6.0 deploy lands; the new file is the authoritative backup.

**Set `NUXT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` on the Pi before restarting** the service. With the CSRF middleware live, an empty allowlist in production rejects every state-changing `/api/*` request with 403. Set to your Tailscale Funnel URL (plus the LAN origin `http://192.168.0.224:3000` if you ever access directly), e.g. `NUXT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://your-funnel.example.com,http://192.168.0.224:3000`. The dev default of `http://localhost:3000` is built in.

**Verify CSP in the browser before flipping `NUXT_CSP_ENFORCE` to `true`.** The first deploy after this PR runs with `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` so violations are visible in the console without breaking the page. Hit all three dashboard charts (donut, cash-flow, daily-spends) and confirm the console is clean. If `unsafe-eval` is required for ECharts formatters, keep it and add a comment in `server/utils/csp.ts` explaining the trade-off. Once clean, set `NUXT_CSP_ENFORCE=true` in the Pi env and restart.
